dispatch_center_observation: An adult collapsed. They do not respond and are breathing normally.
dispatch_center_assistance: A helper is beside you and can bring an AED.
dispatch_center_change: Their breathing has changed to occasional irregular gasps. They still do not respond.
dispatch_center_description: Locate a room and entrance. Report a change in breathing.
dispatch_trail_place: River Loop Trail, Pine Harbor, Maine.
dispatch_trail_access: Trail marker 4, near the footbridge. Access from the Elm Street parking lot.
dispatch_trail_observation: A cyclist fell. They are awake and answering questions, with heavy bleeding from one lower leg.
dispatch_trail_assistance: A helper is applying direct pressure to the wound.
dispatch_trail_change: Blood is now soaking through the dressing. The helper is still applying pressure.
dispatch_trail_description: Use landmarks when there is no street number. Report what has changed.
dispatch_auto_location: My phone will tell you exactly where I am.
dispatch_vague_location: I am somewhere near a building or a trail.
dispatch_text_first_prompt: Begin the practice text with your location and a brief description of the emergency.
dispatch_voice_first_prompt: 911. Where is the emergency? Include the town and how to find you.
dispatch_location_why: Give the town, location, and useful access details. Do not rely only on automatic phone location.
dispatch_text_location_missing: Include the location, access details, and the emergency in the first practice text.
dispatch_voice_location_missing: Add both the location and the room, entrance, or trail access.
dispatch_observations_prompt: What happened? What can you observe, and is anyone helping?
dispatch_guess_diagnosis: I know the diagnosis without checking.
dispatch_guess_age: They are exactly 42 years old, although I have not asked.
dispatch_observations_why: Describe what you see and know. If you do not know an answer, say so.
dispatch_observations_missing: Include the observed condition and the help already available.
dispatch_callback_prompt: What number can I use to reach this phone if we get disconnected?
dispatch_guess_callback: I will make up a number because I cannot remember it.
dispatch_callback_why: The callback number is the phone you are using, not the emergency number.
dispatch_callback_missing: Use the fictional phone number shown in the scene details.
dispatch_change_prompt: A new observation appears. What update do you give the dispatcher now?
dispatch_wait_change: I will wait until the conversation is over to mention the change.
dispatch_change_why: Report a change promptly so the dispatcher can adjust instructions.
dispatch_change_missing: Select the new observation, rather than the earlier condition.
dispatch_text_last_prompt: The practice dispatcher asks you to keep replying and follow the instructions. What do you do?
dispatch_voice_last_prompt: The practice dispatcher asks you to stay on the line and follow the instructions. What do you do?
dispatch_close_early: End the conversation now that I have given the address.
dispatch_text_follow: Keep watching for replies, answer questions, and follow the instructions.
dispatch_voice_follow: Stay on the line, answer questions, and follow the instructions.
dispatch_invent_arrival: Promise the person that an ambulance will arrive in exactly two minutes.
dispatch_connected_why: Stay connected until told to end. Questions and instructions support the response; an arrival time is not yours to promise.
dispatch_connected_missing: Choose how you will continue communicating with the dispatcher.
dispatch_map_caption: Fictional practice map. Use the supplied location details.
dispatch_intro: Choose the facts a dispatcher needs, build a practice response, and adapt when the scene changes. You can speak, sign, or read your response before checking it.
dispatch_text_notice: In Maine, text 911 when a voice call is not possible. Include your location and the emergency in the first message. Text availability varies elsewhere.
dispatch_order_note: Real dispatchers may ask questions in a different order. Follow their instructions. This exercise uses fictional details and has no timer.
dispatch_restart_copy: This saved practice does not contain a complete conversation. Start a new rehearsal to build the review.
dispatch_independent: responses ready on the first check without an example
dispatch_transfer_title: Try the skill away from the screen
dispatch_transfer: With a partner, describe how a responder would find this room or outdoor location. Use speech, writing, sign, or AAC. Then explain which observation you would report first if it changed.
dispatch_transfer_boundary: Keep this as a role-play. Do not place a real emergency call for practice.
dispatch_select_facts: Select every detail needed for this response
dispatch_preview_empty: Your selected details will appear here.
dispatch_remove_guesses: Remove guesses, unsupported promises, or details that do not answer this question.
dispatch_boundary: SIMULATION ONLY · No call or text is sent. All locations and phone numbers below are fictional.
dispatch_reference: Read the voice and text reference scripts
